title: Initial inert extensions of a simplex to its output colors
statement: Use symmetric operadic families and inert edges of [def-coef-symmetric-operadic-family], joins of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone], and coherent join coslices of [lem-cbc-relative-coslice-left-fibration]. Let $M^\otimes\to T\times N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)$ be a small symmetric operadic family, and let $\tau:\Delta^r\to M^\otimes$ end at $d$ over $(t,\langle s\rangle)$. Let $I=\{1,\ldots,s\}$ be discrete and map $\Delta^r\star I$ to $T\times N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)$ using the projection of $\tau$ and the inert color projections $\rho_i:\langle s\rangle\to\langle1\rangle$ of its last vertex; its $T$-coordinate is the $T$-projection of $\tau$ composed with the map $\Delta^r\star I\to\Delta^r$ sending every $i\in I$ to the last vertex $r$, so each edge from the last old vertex to $i$ lies over $(1_t,\rho_i)$. Form $X=M^\otimes\times_{T\times N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)}(\Delta^r\star I)$, let $\bar\tau$ be the lifted initial simplex, let $X_i$ be the fiber over $i\in I$, and put $J_i=X_i\times_X X_{\bar\tau/}$. Each $J_i$ is a quasicategory with an initial object: one is supplied by any extension of $\tau$ whose last edge $d\to d_i$ is a cocartesian inert lift of the $i$th color projection. Such an extension exists. Here initial means that its mapping space to every object of $J_i$ is contractible. The extension category $J=\coprod_iJ_i$ is empty for $s=0$. The assertion holds for arbitrary $r\geq0$ and imposes no limits or colimits in the fibers.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 3.1.2.3, step (3), printed pp.340-341: the categories of extensions of a simplex to its output projections and their initial objects. September 18, 2017 edition inspected online. WANTED: archive in literature/. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical assertion.

proof.text:
Put $C=M^\otimes$, $D=T\times N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)$, and denote the family projection by $p:C\to D$. It is an inner fibration between quasicategories: it is a categorical fibration by [def-coef-symmetric-operadic-family], and every inner horn is a trivial cofibration by [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. For a fixed $i$, write $b_i=(t,\langle1\rangle)$ and $f_i=(1_t,\rho_i):p(d)\to b_i$. Let $\beta_i:\Delta^r\star\Delta^0\to D$ be the restriction of the specified base join map to the output $i$, viewed as a vertex of $D_{p\tau/}$. The coslice formula in [lem-cbc-relative-coslice-left-fibration] identifies
$$J_i=C_{\tau/}\times_{D_{p\tau/}}\{\beta_i\}.$$
Indeed, an $n$-simplex on either side is a map $\Delta^r\star\Delta^n\to C$ restricting to $\tau$ and having base the map obtained from $\beta_i$ by collapsing the whole last block to its cone vertex. On the original pullback $X$, the projection to $\Delta^r\star I$ is forced by its vertices: this join is the nerve of the poset obtained by putting each $i\in I$ after $[r]$. The nerve of this poset is a quasicategory directly: the consecutive edges of an inner horn specify a weakly increasing chain of vertices (for a two-dimensional inner horn use transitivity), and that chain specifies a simplex restricting to every given face, since a poset nerve has at most one simplex with prescribed ordered vertices. Pulling back an inner-horn lifting problem for $X\to\Delta^r\star I$ gives one for $p$, so this pullback map is an inner fibration by [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]; filling the base horn first also shows that $X$ is a quasicategory. Thus the identity fixes all mixed simplices and commutes with every simplicial operator; it is an equality of the prescribed coherent extension models.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 3.1.2.3, step (3), printed pp.340-341, definition of X and its output extension categories; explicit degreewise expansion.

proof.text:
The inclusion $j:\{r\}\hookrightarrow\Delta^r=N([r])$ is full, and for each vertex $a$ the comma category of arrows $a\to j(r)$ is the nerve of the one-object, identity-only category, since there is exactly one arrow $a\to r$. It is therefore a point and weakly contractible. Apply [lem-coef-cofinal-relative-join-slice-restriction] with this $j$, $u=\tau$, and the inner fibration $p$ from step 1. It gives a trivial Kan fibration
$$R:C_{\tau/}\longrightarrow C_{d/}\times_{D_{p(d)/}}D_{p\tau/}.$$
Set $L_i=C_{d/}\times_{D_{p(d)/}}\{f_i\}$. The map $L_i\to C_{d/}\times_{D_{p(d)/}}D_{p\tau/}$ pairs its first coordinate with the constant simplex at $\beta_i$. This is well-defined because restriction of $\beta_i$ to the last old vertex and the cone vertex is $f_i$. Its pullback of $R$ is exactly the restriction $q_i:J_i\to L_i$. Every boundary lifting problem for $q_i$ gives one for $R$; pair the resulting lift with the prescribed simplex of $L_i$. Thus $q_i$ lifts every boundary, including the empty boundary in dimension zero, as in [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration].

source.place: Proposition 2.1.2.5, right-anodyne relative coslice restriction, applied through the existing cofinal restriction lemma to the terminal vertex of a simplex; HA proof p.341 initial-output assertion expanded.

proof.text: By [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality], $L_i$ is a quasicategory. To see that $J_i$ is a quasicategory, project an inner horn in it to $L_i$, fill there, then lift that simplex relative to the original horn using $q_i$. The latter lift is justified by [lem-coef-infinity-monomorphism-boundary-cells]: a horn inclusion is a monomorphism and hence is built from boundary inclusions; solve the boundary lifting problems of $q_i$ one at a time, and take the union of the compatible solutions. This uses exactly the boundary lifting established in step 2 and the definition in [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration]. Now [def-coef-symmetric-operadic-family] supplies a $p$-cocartesian lift $e_i:d\to d_i$ of $f_i$ within the fiber at $t$, since $\rho_i$ is inert. It is a vertex of $L_i$, and the dimension-zero lifting property of $q_i$ gives a vertex $B_i$ over it. This vertex is an extension of the entire original $\tau$ over the fixed $\beta_i$, with last edge exactly $e_i$. No existence of lifts over any other base edges is used.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 3.1.2.3, printed p.341, existence of initial output extensions; relative coslice boundary lifting gives exact extension of the fixed simplex.

proof.text: Let $B\in J_i$ be any vertex whose last edge $e=q_i(B)$ is $p$-cocartesian over $f_i$. The initial-lift clause of [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality] makes $e$ initial in $L_i$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-relative-initial-boundary] to $L_i\to\Delta^0$: for every $n>0$, every boundary $\partial\Delta^n\to L_i$ with first vertex $e$ extends. Given a boundary $a:\partial\Delta^n\to J_i$ with first vertex $B$, extend $q_i a$ in $L_i$, and lift this extension through $q_i$ relative to $a$, using [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration] and step 2. Hence all positive-dimensional boundaries in $J_i$ beginning at $B$ extend. Applying [lem-coef-infinity-relative-initial-boundary] to $J_i\to\Delta^0$ now proves that $\operatorname{Map}_{J_i}(B,Z)\to\Delta^0$ is a weak homotopy equivalence for every $Z\in J_i$. These spaces are contractible, which is precisely the required initiality. Both uses of the boundary criterion are legal because the domain is a quasicategory by step 3, so its map to a point is an inner fibration.

source.place: Corollary 7.1.5.17, positive-boundary criterion, applied twice to expand the initiality assertion in HA proof of Theorem 3.1.2.3, printed p.341; HTT Remark 2.4.1.9, cocartesian dual.

proof.text: Steps 3 and 4 show existence and initiality for each output and for every choice of cocartesian final edge. If $r=0$, the inclusion $\{r\}\hookrightarrow\Delta^r$ in step 2 is the identity and $q_i$ is the identity of $L_i$, so step 3 supplies the inert lift as an object of this very category, and step 4 proves its initiality directly there. If $s=0$, there are no indices $i$, and the degreewise coproduct $J=\coprod_{i\in\varnothing}J_i$ is empty in every degree. The argument used only inert edge lifts, relative coslice restriction, and horn and boundary lifting; it imposed no limit or colimit condition on any fiber.

split_report.summary: Expanded the inert-output extension argument into exact relative coslice restriction to the final vertex, existence by zero-dimensional lifting, and initiality by positive-boundary lifting. Reused existing cofinal restriction, cocartesian lift initiality and boundary calculus; created no nodes. Corrected the introductory slice citation to the coslice definition actually used, with no mathematical statement change. Checked r=0 and s=0 and retained the fixed base cone throughout. Second reading expanded the elementary poset-nerve horn filler and the r=0 conclusion, and independently repeated semantic and source searches.
split_report.blueprint: Historical ancestor prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint, proof paragraph 2 derived coefficient-adjunction infrastructure, through lem-coef-symmetric-operadic-left-horn-filling. Current main-20261015 proof has no separate operadic substep. Steps 1-4 expand HA proof of Theorem 3.1.2.3 step (3), pp.340-341, initial objects in each output component; step 5 handles the empty output and vertex cases.

tool_uses.why: Step 1 uses its degreewise coherent join-coslice construction as a generic simplicial tool, filed in sk-prop-sf-cbc. The item unit has no alternate coslice construction; this is notation and infrastructure and does not replace a step of its geometric proof route.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q64-6a19566ce (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item, all 3 statement deps, all 9 proof deps and the one citer in full. All five steps are correct. Step 1: the join Δ^r⋆I is a poset nerve, so the map to it is forced degreewise and J_i = C_{τ/}×_{D_{pτ/}}{β_i} exactly. Step 2: {r}⊂Δ^r is full and every comma of arrows a→r is Δ^0, so the coslice clause (not the dual) of lem-coef-cofinal-relative-join-slice-restriction applies; its pullback gives q_i: J_i→L_i=L(d,f_i), a trivial Kan fibration. Step 3: J_i is a quasicategory by the boundary-cell lifting; the inert lift from the family definition lies within M_t^⊗, so over (1_t,ρ_i), and q_i is surjective on vertices, which gives existence. Step 4: lem-coef-infinity-relative-initial-boundary is used twice over Δ^0 and proves initiality for every extension with a cocartesian last edge. Step 5: r=0, s=0, s=1 and degenerate τ checked. One fault fixed: the old statement fixed the new vertices at T-coordinate t but left the T-edge r→i free. For a general quasicategory T that edge need not be an equivalence, and then the existence clause can fail. The proof uses f_i=(1_t,ρ_i). The fix states that the T-coordinate is pr_T(pτ) composed with the collapse Δ^r⋆I→Δ^r (i↦r). This is forced in the only citer, where T=Δ^m. No hypothesis or conclusion is otherwise changed. Corrected file: fixes/dag/nodes/sec-six-functors/lem-coef-symmetric-family-inert-cone-initiality.json. HA Thm 3.1.2.3 pp.340-341 is not archived locally, so I could not open it; I recognise the claim and verified it entirely through DAG statements. No SGA source is used. The duplicate grep (inert/initial/color projection/3.1.2.3) found no duplicate. There are no new nodes.
